name: wikipediatrend
what_it_holds: R package (GPL>=2, v2.1.6 released 2020-06-03) with wp_trend() to retrieve per-article Wikipedia pageview time series by language/article, returning a tidy date/lang/article/views data frame. Critically, it stitches together historical pre-2016 data (pre-dating the official API, sourced from a Hertie School of Governance-commissioned archive hosted at petermeissner.de) with the post-2016 official Wikimedia Foundation API, giving continuous coverage back to as early as 2007-2008 for some articles.
why_useful: Fills the point-in-time/history-depth problem directly: our stated gap is that Google Trends pulls are not point-in-time and pageviews tooling generally starts in 2015. This gives longer (2007+) continuous history for city/destination/attraction Wikipedia articles as a demand proxy usable for longer backtests than the official API alone allows.
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Fills the point-in-time/history-depth problem directly: our stated gap is that Google Trends pulls are not point-in-time and pageviews tooling generally starts in 2015. This gives longer (2007+) continuous history for city/destination/attraction Wikipedia articles as a demand proxy usable for longer backtests than the official API alone allows.

name: common-crawl-ranks-cache
what_it_holds: Daily-polled (effectively quarterly, since CC webgraph releases are quarterly) mirror of Common Crawl's host- and domain-level web-graph ranks, Top-1M per release. Host-level CSV: rank, harmonic-centrality score, PageRank position, PageRank value, hostname. Domain-level CSV adds distinct-host count per domain. Gzip-compressed CSVs in a GitHub Actions-driven repo; no stated start date/backfill (tracks only from first cron run), license 'Other'.
why_useful: Directly answers gap 5 (web-traffic/engagement proxies: Tranco/Common Crawl host-graph ranks). If airbnb.com (and Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia domains) sit inside the Top-1M, this gives a free, repeatable time series of relative web-graph prominence per CC quarterly release that could proxy for site engagement/traffic momentum, complementing the missing Similarweb/Cloudflare Radar data.
time_coverage: from first cron run (recent) forward, refreshed ~quarterly with CC webgraph releases
size_hint: Top-1M hosts/domains per release, gzip CSV
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Directly answers gap 5 (web-traffic/engagement proxies: Tranco/Common Crawl host-graph ranks). If airbnb.com (and Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia domains) sit inside the Top-1M, this gives a free, repeatable time series of relative web-graph prominence per CC quarterly release that could proxy for site engagement/traffic momentum, complementing the missing Similarweb/Cloudflare Radar data.

name: Tranco top-sites list
what_it_holds: Research-grade top-1M-sites domain ranking aggregated from Cisco Umbrella, Majestic, Farsight, Chrome UX Report (CrUX), and Cloudflare Radar, averaged over rolling 30-day windows; historical daily list IDs are permanently retrievable (point-in-time by construction), with Python/Go client libraries and a GitHub source repo (linked from the site) plus BigQuery access. Not Common-Crawl-derived, but sits in the same 'host popularity ranking' space as cc-webgraph and is more directly comparable to Similarweb/CrUX-rank asks in gap 5.
why_useful: Gives a genuinely point-in-time (dated list IDs, never revised) domain-popularity series for airbnb.com vs booking.com/expedia.com/vrbo.com going back years, filling gap 5's 'Tranco / host-graph rank' ask directly and with an off-the-shelf client.
time_coverage: Tranco lists generated daily since ~2018, each permanently archived by ID
size_hint: each list ~1M domains, small compressed CSV per date

name: google-play-scraper (JoMingyu)
what_it_holds: Python library for pulling Google Play Store app metadata, ratings, rating-count histories, and full review text/timestamps for any app ID via public endpoints (no scraping of restricted pages), handling pagination beyond the 200-review batch limit. Generic tool, not Airbnb-specific, but trivially pointed at the Airbnb Android app package to pull rating trend and dated user reviews.
why_useful: A clean, general-purpose, non-Airbnb-site method to build an Airbnb app rating/review-count time series as an engagement/usage proxy -- directly addresses gap #5 (app rankings/engagement history) without touching airbnb.com, so it is not a rule-6 ToS question the way a direct Airbnb-site scraper would be.
